name: inprocess-obi-wb-uart-zipdma-route-write-f1f6
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU with one real Wishbone-classic ZipCPU UART and a ZipDMA: the master pushes the RAM source block into the UART TXREG through the UART's own cyc/stb/ack Wishbone cycle, and the case line states the sampled we/adr/dat_w/dat_r and the target's own ack count.

evidence.source: third_party/soc-zipcpu-wbuart/rtl/wbuart.v:119-137 (uart_setup is written from the four byte lanes of UART_SETUP) and 513 (a read of UART_SETUP returns {1'b0, uart_setup}), so the word the master pushed last is the word the CPU reads back

notes: the routed register is SETUP (offset 0x00) and the declared evidence is SETUP itself: the RTL stores the four byte lanes of the write into the 31-bit uart_setup register and a read returns {1'b0, uart_setup} (wbuart.v:119-137,513), so the CPU's readback after the transfer is exactly the last word the master pushed.  A TXREG (offset 0x0c) write route was tried first and its evidence is NOT admissible: the whole-word FIFO_STATUS readback does not change across a four-word push because the pinned transmitter drains one entry per push (ufifo.v i_rd=(!tx_busy)&&empty_n), so 'the evidence word changed' would be a false witness; this scenario therefore routes SETUP and states that fact here
the four routed beats present the same fixed target address, so the last one wins: the RAM source block (the F6 record's words) is the data the master pushes

the routed target is the pinned ZipCPU wbuart Wishbone-classic slave behind the generated beat_to_wishbone adapter; its register window is 16 bytes and its profile declares SETUP 0 (rw, a write resets the UART state), FIFO_STATUS 4 (ro), RXREG 8 (rw, a read pops the RX FIFO) and TXREG 12 (rw, a write pushes the TX FIFO)

the target is mapped at 0x20005000 rather than its SoC 0x40001000 because the pinned ZipDMA's SOURCE/DESTINATION CSR fields are 30-bit byte addresses (third_party/soc-zipcpu/rtl/zipdma/zipdma_ctrl.v:73-74,161-181,259-260 with ADDRESS_WIDTH=32, BUS_WIDTH=32): a byte address >= 0x40000000 cannot be encoded
the RAM source block is the four input words the F6 record carries, so the pushed bytes are the record's own data
F6 is the only routed flow here: with no behavior file the UART declares no F5 facts, so F5 is refused by name and F1-F4/F6 stay available
